findings.claim: Fable 5.1 cache reads cut 75% to $0.25 per million tokens; input/output unchanged at $10/$50 per MTok; Anthropic estimates ~25% typical and up to ~45% highly agentic savings from August 2026 usage mix.
gpt-6-astra short-context standard list is $10 input / $1.00 cached / $50 output per MTok; Fast mode table lists $20 / $2.00 / $100 — 2× standard on those meters.

Gemini 3.8 Flash ships at intro $0.75/$3.75 per MTok input/output; introductory price expires Dec 31, 2026; from Jan 1, 2027 rates become $1.50/$7.50. Google states the model 'works harder' and may use more tokens.

Paid Standard Gemini 3.8 Flash: $0.75 input / $3.75 output through Dec 31, 2026 then $1.50/$7.50; context caching $0.075 through Dec 31, 2026 then $0.15 (plus storage). Pricing page last updated 2026-09-15 UTC.

Independent DeepSWE v1.1 same harness (mini-swe-agent): GPT-6 Astra XHigh and Gemini 3.8 Flash High both 74% pass; published average task cost $6.52 vs $2.36 with ~30k vs ~143k output tokens per task (Aeon Model Economics Lab 2026-09-04 compilation of the same leaderboard). Claude Fable 5.1 is not present as a DeepSWE point in that compilation (leaderboard HTML shows claude-fable-5, not 5.1).

Artificial Analysis: Fable 5.1 (max) costs $3.76 per Intelligence Index task vs Fable 5 (max) $3.14 (~20% higher) because ~1.7× output tokens; cache-read cut saves ~$1.40/task and is concentrated where majority of input tokens are cache reads. Effort span 13.1M–143.7M output tokens (low→max) across the Index.

Firecrawl measured 57 API-billed runs: on sandboxed agentic builds one Fable 5.1 run re-read 1.69M cached tokens for $0.42 vs a Fable 5 run re-reading 1.34M for $1.34; mean-of-2 builds show ~2.10M–2.13M cache re-reads with Fable 5.1 bill ~$7.00 vs Fable 5 ~$6.88 (output tokens still largest line). Savings on those builds 15–30% of bill, below Anthropic's 25–45% headline because cache writes stay $20/MTok.

Superpower Daily evidence-matrix (v2 JSON dataset): if every Fable reuse hits and every Gemini implicit reuse misses, Fable five-minute cache becomes cheaper at 24 reuses (one-hour at 39). If Gemini caches ≥74.074% of reuse tokens, Fable cannot undercut on prefix economics under a single successful write. Derived from Primary rate cards; not a measured production hit-rate panel across vendors.

Real-SWE (Specific Labs, ~10 tasks × 8 runs): native-harness cost-per-resolved-task ~$17.94 Fable 5.1/Claude Code, ~$13.82 Astra/Codex CLI, ~$8.01 Gemini 3.8 Flash/Gemini CLI. Explicitly NOT same-harness; authors do not disclose whether prompt caching entered cost estimates. Useful as production-shaped economics, not as the three-lane same-harness receipt.

VendorBenchmark 2026 GenAI cost benchmark (cohort medians): copilot/seat licenses 38–52% of GenAI budget vs API consumption 22–38%. Hybrid seat+meter structures are common; does not prove Primary procurement that default agentic production lanes treat API list price as inert.

OpenAI Help Center: new ChatGPT Enterprise agreements may use token-based USD billing for Work/Codex usage (input/cached/output), not seats-only; credit-based plans remain for other cohorts. Cuts against a clean 'list price inert / seats only' kill of Leg A for agentic production.

Gradually.ai Fable 5.1 vs Gemini 3.8 Flash page verifies list prices ($10/$50 vs $0.75/$3.75; cache read $0.25 vs $0.075) as of 2026-09-02 but reports zero directly matched shared benchmark series and incomplete same-prompt test coverage (Gemini unavailable on one visual test).

Esso.dev Sep 2026 synthesis: Fable cache-read cut changes agent bills; Gemini same token price but ~40% higher real cost/task per Artificial Analysis vs 3.7; Astra vendor harness claims contested. Frames Leg A vs Leg B tension without new Primary share or three-lane same-harness measurements.

recommendation_detail: Primary pricing pages still corroborate all three board numbers (Fable cache $0.25/M, Astra Fast 2×, Gemini intro cliff→double), so pricing_contradiction kill fails. Path-2 kill_LegA also fails: no Primary procurement share shows default agentic lanes chosen by seats/credits with list price inert, and OpenAI's token-based Enterprise rate card cuts the other way. Path-1 succeeds enough to upgrade the Contested falsify surface: Specialist DeepSWE same-harness token-intensity/cost (Astra ~30k/$6.52 vs Flash ~143k/$2.36 at tied 74%), Specialist AA Fable output-intensity (~1.7× vs Fable 5; $3.76/task despite cache cut), and Specialist Firecrawl measured cache re-read volumes on agentic builds. Hold is no longer justified as 'no intensity evidence,' but three-lane same-harness cost-per-task including Fable 5.1 remains an open gap.
gaps: No independent same-harness cost-per-task that jointly includes Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 3.8 Flash (DeepSWE has Astra+Flash; Fable 5.1 appears on AA Coding Agent Index / other suites, not the DeepSWE mini-swe-agent panel used for that pair).
No Primary enterprise procurement/share series proving default agentic production lanes are seat/credit-selected with API list price inert.

No measured cross-vendor production cache-hit-rate panel for the three lanes (Superpower Daily crossover is rate-card math conditional on assumed Gemini hit fractions; Firecrawl/wmedia measure Claude-side cache volumes only).
Real-SWE cost columns are native-harness and do not disclose caching in cost estimation — cannot close the same-harness blind spot.
